H2341.d: Chavilah, the name of two or three eastern regions; also perhaps of two men
fb: Genesis puts it near the rivers of Eden and calls it rich in gold. The name turns up in two different family lines, so it may be two places.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Cush's son in Genesis 10:7. The same name is also a land rich in gold by Eden's rivers, and a son of Joktan, so it may cover more than one region.
Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.
The Tigris, under its Hebrew name. It is one of the four rivers out of Eden, running east of Assyria, and Daniel is standing on its bank when his last vision comes.
Woman living at the time before the Flood

The first woman, made from Adam's rib as a fit companion, and named the mother of all the living. The serpent deceived her into eating from the one forbidden tree, and Adam ate too. Paul later sets that against the obedience of Christ.

H2351.d: properly, separate by a wall, i.e. outside, outdoors

H2320.d: the new moon; by implication, a month

H2340.d: a Chivvite, one of the aboriginal tribes of Palestine
fb: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

H2343.d: Chul, a son of Aram; also the region settled by him
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Aram's son, Shem's grandson, in the Table of Nations. Like the other names there it probably means a clan or district. Its location is not known.

H2308.d: properly, to be flabby, i.e. (by implication) desist; (figuratively) be lacking or idle

fb: North of Damascus. It marks how far Abram chased the four kings who had taken Lot, after routing them at night near Dan. Nobody has matched it to a modern site.

H2339.d: a string; by implication, a measuring tape

H2388.d: to fasten upon; hence, to seize, be strong (figuratively, courageous, causatively strengthen, cure, help, repair, fortify), obstinate; to bind, restrain, conquer

H2398.d: properly, to miss; hence (figuratively and generally) to sin; by inference, to forfeit, lack, expiate, repent, (causatively) lead astray, condemn

fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Nahor and Milcah had him, one of the sons who became Aramean clans. Nahor was Abraham's brother.
Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
A son of Ishmael, in the list of Genesis 25:15. Nothing else is told of him.
King living at the time of the Patriarchs
He was king of Edom in the days before Israel had any king.

H2347.d: properly, to cover, i.e. (figuratively) to compassionate

H2366.d: Chushim, the name of three Israelites
fb: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of the wives of a Benjamite clan leader in the Chronicles genealogy. The same name belongs to a son of Dan.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Hushim. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

H2389.d: strong (usu. in a bad sense, hard, bold, violent)

H2354.d: Chur, the name of four Israelites and one Midianite
fb: Aaron's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
He helped Aaron hold up Moses's arms while Israel fought Amalek, since Israel won as long as those hands stayed up. When Moses went up Sinai for the law, Hur was left in charge with Aaron.
King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Numbers and Joshua name him twice, and he is a king from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Hur. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.

H2372.d: to gaze at; mentally to perceive, contemplate (with pleasure); specifically, to have a vision of

H2373.d: the breast (as most seen in front)

H2397.d: a ring for the nose (or lips)

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Benjamin's son, and the Huphamite clan in the wilderness census comes from him. Genesis and Chronicles call him Huppim.

H2350.d: a Chuphamite or descendant of Chupham
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
They were Hupham's clan, counted in the census of Numbers 26.

H2363.d: to hurry; figuratively, to be eager with excitement or enjoyment

H2333.d: by implication, an encampment or village

H2342.d: properly, to twist or whirl (in a circular or spiral manner), i.e. (specifically) to dance, to writhe in pain (especially of parturition) or fear; figuratively, to wait, to pervert

fb: A lowland town of Judah, in the district with Lachish. The name means new, and it is never mentioned again.

H2330.d: properly, to tie a knot, i.e. (figuratively) to propound a riddle

H2377.d: a sight (mentally), i.e. a dream, revelation, or oracle

H2318.d: to be new; causatively, to rebuild

H2337.d: a dell or crevice (as if pierced in the earth)

fb: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy

David's friend, who stayed behind when Absalom rebelled so he could work from inside Absalom's court. Ahithophel gave Absalom sound advice, Hushai talked him into a worse plan, and the time it bought saved David.

H2374.d: a beholder in vision; also a compact (as looked upon with approval)

fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

King of Aram-Damascus. He was father of Tabrimon and grandfather of the Ben-hadad whom Asa paid to attack Israel. Some identify him with Rezon, who set up the Damascus kingdom against Solomon, but the link is not certain.
King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

Elijah was told to anoint him king of Aram, and the prophet wept over what Hazael would do to Israel. He smothered his own king to get the throne and was one of Israel's worst enemies for decades. An inscription with his name has been found in Damascus.

H2336.d: a thorn; by analogy, a ring for the nose

H2396.d: Chizkijah, a king of Judah, also the name of two other Israelites
fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

One of Judah's few good kings. He came after Ahaz, reopened the temple, tore down the high places, and broke up the bronze serpent Moses had made once people began worshipping it. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC, Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah promised deliverance, and the siege broke overnight. His seal impression has been dug up near the Temple Mount, and his tunnel still runs under the city.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra and Nehemiah name him twice, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Zephaniah is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 4 men called Hezekiah. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One name in Judah's genealogy, tied to the descendants of Ezer.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

A Gadite in Bashan, east of the Jordan, and father of Abihail. Gad's genealogy runs through him down to family heads in the days of Jotham of Judah and Jeroboam II of Israel. Nothing else is recorded about him.

H2369.d: Chotham, the name of two Israelites
fb: Heber's son, of Beriah's clan and a chief in Asher; another Hotham turns up among David's warriors.
Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years.

H2361.d: Churam, the name of an Israelite and two Syrians
fb: King living at the time of United Monarchy
Chronicles spells the king of Tyre this way. He is the Hiram who sent materials for Solomon's temple.
Syrian living at the time of United Monarchy
The bronzeworker the king of Tyre sent to make the temple's furnishings, spelled Huram in Chronicles and Hiram elsewhere.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
One of 3 men called Huram. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Shaharaim sent away two wives, Hushim and Baara, and had sons in Moab by others. Hodesh was one of them, and she is named so her sons, heads of Benjamite families, could be recorded.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Benjamite descended from Elpaal, in the Chronicles genealogy, and that is the whole entry.
Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
Chronicles' name for one of David's thirty, from the valley by Mount Gaash in Ephraim. Samuel's list calls him Hiddai.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
He was a Gershonite Levite, through Shimei, in the lists David drew up for temple service.

H2387.d: Chezir, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

Head of the seventeenth of the priestly divisions David set up for temple service. A first-century BC tomb in the Kidron Valley names a priestly family called the Sons of Hezir, so the name stayed in Jerusalem's priesthood a long time.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant. The seventeenth priestly division under David carries the name too.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
An Ephraimite, named only as father of Amasa, one of four Ephraimite chiefs who stood in front of the returning army and made them release and care for the Judean captives.
Exiles back from Babylon resettled it, a Benjamin town grouped with Lod and Ono in the lists. It is el-Haditheh, a few miles east of Lydda.

H2338.d: to string together, i.e. (figuratively) to repair

H2370.d: to gaze upon; mentally to dream, be usual (i.e. seem)

fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man of Judah from the Shilonite clan, Shelah's line, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile. Nothing else is recorded about him.

H2331.d: properly, to live; by implication (intensively) to declare or show

H2300.d: to be (causatively, make) sharp or (figuratively) severe

H2352.d: the crevice of a serpent; the cell of a prison

H2380.d: a look; hence (figuratively) striking appearance, revelation, or (by implication) compact

H2309.d: rest, i.e. the state of the dead

H2314.d: properly, to inclose (as a room), i.e. (by analogy,) to beset (as in a siege)

H2362.d: Chavran, a region East of the Jordan
fb: Cave-land, the fertile east of Bashan, named in Ezekiel's boundaries for the land to come. The Greeks and Romans called it Auranitis, centred on Bosra, and its basalt buildings still stand.

H2325.d: properly, perhaps to tie, i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) to owe, or (by implication) to forfeit

fb: A region in Syria between Hamath and Damascus, first on the list in Zechariah 9:1. The Zakkur Stele, an eighth-century BC inscription, names a capital called Hazrach that is almost certainly the same place.
